theory.definition: Narrative Text is a text that tells a story of connected events. In retail, it focuses on inspirational business origins, retail brand histories, and entrepreneurship challenges to entertain and inspire readers.

genericStructure.heading: Orientation
genericStructure.detail: Introduces the business founder, setting, and starting time.

genericStructure.heading: Complication
genericStructure.detail: Describes the main business problem, crisis, or challenge faced.

genericStructure.heading: Resolution
genericStructure.detail: Explains how the founder solved the problem creatively.

genericStructure.heading: Re-orientation
genericStructure.detail: Shows the final success and the moral lesson of the story.

languageFeatures.heading: Time Connectives
languageFeatures.detail: e.g., long ago, at first, suddenly, finally.

sections.heading: ORIENTATION
sections.body: Long ago in 1943, a 17-year-old boy named Ingvar Kamprad founded a small mail-order business in Sweden. He named it IKEA, using his initials (I.K.) plus the first letters of Elmtaryd and Agunnaryd, the farm and village where he grew up. At first, he sold small household items like pens, wallets, and picture frames.

sections.heading: COMPLICATION
sections.body: As IKEA grew and began selling affordable furniture, local traditional furniture store owners became furious. They pressured suppliers to BOYCOTT Kamprad, preventing him from receiving pre-assembled furniture. Furthermore, shipping large wooden tables and sofas was extremely EXPENSIVE and often resulted in damaged goods during DELIVERY. Kamprad faced a major crisis that threatened to close his growing business.

sections.heading: RESOLUTION
sections.body: Instead of giving up, Kamprad and his designer came up with a REVOLUTIONARY idea: "FLAT-PACKING." They decided to disassemble a table by taking off its legs so it could fit into a flat box. Customers would buy the boxed furniture and ASSEMBLE it themselves at home. This innovation drastically reduced shipping costs, saved store warehouse space, and allowed IKEA to sell high-quality furniture at unbelievably low prices.

sections.heading: RE-ORIENTATION
sections.body: Today, IKEA has grown into the world's largest furniture RETAILER with hundreds of stores worldwide. Ingvar Kamprad proved that facing business challenges with creativity and customer-focused solutions can turn a local struggle into a global success story.
